item.title: “The Democratic Party Never Even Holds a Discussion on Polarization… Is It Really the Party of the Middle Class and Ordinary People?” (“민주당, 양극화 토론 한번을 안해…중산층·서민의 정당 맞나”)
item.description:
Ahead of the Democratic Party of Korea’s August 17 national convention, a debate over “orthodox lineage” has erupted among the party leadership candidates. One might wonder, “This isn’t a monarchy, so why this talk of orthodox lineage?” Yet, in reality, the current Democratic Party does not have many lawmakers who have consistently stood by the party since the days of President Kim Dae-jung’s Peace Democratic Party (PDP). While this is partly a natural change over time, it also reflects the Democratic Party’s tumultuous history of repeated splits and mergers. (더불어민주당의 8·17 전당대회를 앞두고 당대표 후보들 사이에서 ‘적통’ 논쟁이 벌어졌다. ‘왕조시대도 아닌데 웬 적통 논쟁인가’ 싶은데, 정작 지금의 민주당엔 김대중 대통령의 평화민주당(평민당) 시절부터 당을 꾸준히 지켜온 의원들이 의외로 많지도 않다. 세월 흐름에 따른 자연스러운 변화이기도 하지만, 분당과 통합을 반복하며 부침이 많았던 민주당의 사정이 반영된 결과이기도 할 것이다.)

Lawmaker Woo Won-shik (five-term) is a living witness to this history of the Democratic Party. After leading a movement to oust former President Chun Doo-hwan and engaging in labor activism in Seoul’s Guro-dong area, he joined the Peace Democratic Party in 1988. Except for a brief period when he was elected Speaker of the 22nd National Assembly and temporarily stepped down from his party affiliation, he has spent 38 years continuously with the Democratic Party. ( 우원식 의원(5선)은 이런 민주당의 역사를 지켜본 산증인이다. 전두환 전 대통령 퇴진 운동을 벌이고 서울 구로동 등에서 노동운동을 하다 1988년 평화민주당에 입당한 그는 22대 국회 전반기 국회의장에 선출돼 잠시 당적을 내려놓은 걸 제외하곤 38년을 줄곧 민주당과 함께 했다. )

Meeting at the National Assembly Members’ Office Building on the 16th, when candidate registration for the Democratic Party’s national convention began, Woo expressed feeling “more frustrated and burdened than ever.” “It’s only been a year since we overcame the life-threatening crisis of an illegal martial law and insurrection with the people, and the Lee Jae-myung administration was established,” yet internal divisions have led to name-calling and talk of a “Myeong-Cheong War” (referring to a power struggle between factions), presenting an image of “internal power struggles.” He said, “I hear people saying that they don’t know who the Democratic Party is for anymore,” adding, “If the people’s disappointment grows and we fail (to regain power), I fear we might never be able to form a democratic government again.” <<> ―The race for the national convention has begun. What kind of image should the candidates show in this convention? <<> “After the impeachment of President Park Geun-hye, the people gave us power, but (due to our shortcomings) we lost it in just five years. Then, through the impeachment of President Yoon Suk-yeol, (the people) gave the Democratic Party another chance, but within a year of taking office, the people’s lives are regressing. Yet, the party is only showing power struggles. Going through the June 3 local elections, I felt ‘the Democratic Party is showing a face far removed from the people’s expectations.’ If the ‘4th Democratic Government’ fails due to internal division... then who would trust the Democratic Party and rally again to create a democratic government in the future? The next time will be truly difficult. This convention must create a very important opportunity for change, with that sense of urgency, to reshape a new Democratic Party that is closer to the people.” <<> ―You recently reminded people via Facebook that the Democratic Party aims to be “the party of the middle class and ordinary people, a national party.” What is the current state of the Democratic Party? <<> “Look at how difficult life is for the middle class and ordinary people now. The delinquency rate for small business owners’ loans has risen by 12%, and the average real estate price in Seoul has surpassed 1 billion won. On one hand, semiconductors are thriving and stock prices have surged, but those gains have not yet reached (the majority of) the people. Rather, the gap is widening, worsening polarization. Yet, I’ve never heard the Democratic Party, a ‘party of the middle class and ordinary people,’ raise polarization as an agenda item. Over the past year, it seems all we’ve done is push for prosecutorial and judicial reform. Also, amid growing concerns about the crisis of local extinction, the government brought forward an agenda for metropolitan integration, but the Democratic Party had no role in it. Even now, candidates running in the national convention talk about ‘what I’ve done in South Jeolla’ or ‘what I’ve done in Gwangju,’ but you rarely hear ‘what I’ve done in Busan or North Gyeongsang.’ That’s because party member votes are all concentrated in the Honam region.” <<> ―Yet, at the convention, the ‘abolition of prosecutors’ supplementary investigative powers’ seems to be the biggest topic. <<> “The issue of supplementary investigative powers is about how to prevent harm to citizens that could arise from the police’s exclusive exercise of power when prosecutorial investigative powers are abolished, and it’s a matter of providing a clear alternative to reassure the people. But now, this issue has become a campaign strategy for the convention. It’s as if nothing matters unless ‘complete abolition of supplementary investigative powers’ is achieved. Even proposing ‘let’s deliberate on alternatives’ is treated as problematic, which closes off room for dialogue. I’m very worried about how the people might see us.” <<> ―On this issue, even supporters are divided and fighting as ‘Old Democratic Party’ vs. ‘New Lee Jae-myung.’ <<> “During President Kim Dae-jung’s era, many people from the conservative side joined the party. They were given key positions, like National Intelligence Service Director Lee Jong-chan or Presidential Chief of Staff Kim Joong-kwon. They didn’t go anywhere else afterward. They became one with the Democratic Party while realizing their own philosophies. (After the presidential election) New people who joined the party also did so because they agreed with the Democratic Party’s values. So, I don’t understand why we are dividing into factions and constantly trying to split the party internally. We need to consider that President Lee Jae-myung lost once and won once (in the last two presidential elections). Looking at the ‘progressive reform camp vs. conservative reactionary camp’ structure, it’s a difference of just over 1%. Last time, we lost because we were divided; this time, they were divided, so we won. Of course, when bringing in (new figures), we should go through a careful discussion process, but once they are inside, we should discuss differences internally and go through a process of becoming one. But what’s the situation now? Strangely, aren’t we using social media (SNS) to assert our opinions from outside the party, dividing into factions, and engaging in power struggles? If we keep dividing with ‘you’re different from me,’ what will be left? This way, we’ll fail. We’ll never be able to hold power permanently.” <<> ―At the convention, party member sovereignty is being emphasized. The intent seems to be to better reflect the people’s voices in setting the party’s agenda, but there are also criticisms that the party is being overly swayed by the voices of hardline supporters. <<> “Expanding party members’ participation and authority is something a democratic party should naturally do. However, to properly reflect the people’s voices, there needs to be sufficient debate (on issues), but currently, the Democratic Party has no process of deliberation. It’s only about voting. As a result, instead of finding a ‘line’ of agreement, we repeatedly see conflicts and clashes when opinions don’t match.” <<> ―During the convention process, the issue of handling the special counsel bill on fabricated indictments, which grants the authority to withdraw indictments, is likely to become a point of contention. <<> “Illegal issues arising from prosecutorial investigations—whether there were fabrications or coercion—must be clearly revealed through a special counsel to set an example. However, there seems to be significant public disagreement over whether to grant the special counsel the authority to withdraw indictments. That part requires sufficient and careful social discussion. Ultimately, if the fabrication of the indictment is revealed, wouldn’t the court handle it appropriately?” <<> ―Whether to focus on ‘consolidating the core support base’ or ‘expanding the party’s appeal’ is also a key issue at the convention. In particular, it feels like the confrontation is growing larger after writer Yoo Si-min said President Lee Jae-myung’s ‘structural majority’ comment “will inevitably fail.” <<> “I think Yoo might have overexpressed it. He seems to have interpreted the President’s ‘structural majority’ comment as meaning an artificial restructuring of the political landscape (like in the past), but can we actually do an artificial political realignment by allying with people like Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon or Reform Party leader Lee Jun-seok right now? After the insurrection, the People Power Party has actually become even more far-right. The President’s comment probably meant that continuing our centrist reformist and pragmatic approach and improving the people’s lives will ultimately lead to forming a majority. Of course, to achieve a structural majority, we must also continue the path of the grand democratic alliance.” <<> ―In the by-election for Pyeongtaek B district in Gyeonggi Province, the Democratic Party fielded a candidate simultaneously with the Rebuilding Korea Party. Hasn’t that made discussions on the grand democratic alliance and the merger of the two parties more difficult? <<> “In the last general election, the broader opposition, including the Democratic Party, secured a maximum of 192 seats. This was possible because we pursued the grand democratic alliance—‘let the party take the local districts and the proportional coalition take the proportional seats’—despite internal opposition. Because of this, we were able to lift the December 3 martial law and impeach (Yoon Suk-yeol). The grand democratic alliance is essential for winning the presidential election as well, and structuring the election in Pyeongtaek B so that both parties field candidates was a huge mistake. Some say it’s because the merger fell through before the election, but the ultimate responsibility lies with the party leader. Regardless, the issue of merging with the Rebuilding Korea Party must fully reflect the will of members from both sides. There are ways to work together: merger, electoral alliance, or policy coalition. We need to listen carefully to the members and choose which method is best. But we must never lose sight of the grand democratic alliance perspective.” <<> <<> ―There’s also criticism that “young people in their 20s and 30s are turning away from the Democratic Party.” <<> “First, diagnosing (the reason) as ‘young people have become conservative’ is wrong. How would you explain the young people in Daegu, a conservative area, who voted for candidate Kim Boo-kyum? Young people have a huge anxiety about the future. Polarization in our society is intensifying recently, and among the youth, the problem is even more severe. Just looking at the asset gap right now, the largest gap between the top 20% and bottom 20% is among the youth. (The fact that young people are leaving the Democratic Party) I see as them raising an issue about this. It’s not just about listening to their voices; we need to present solutions.” <<> ―During the process of setting the convention rules, the introduction of an elected youth supreme council member position fell through. Young candidates in the convention are also criticizing it as ‘vested-interest politics’ and demanding generational change. <<> “Creating a foundation for younger generations to actively engage in the party is important. In that sense, having party members elect a youth supreme council member provides (an important channel for) elevating youth. Defeating that motion really showed the party as a vested-interest party, a truly ‘old-school’ party. It’s truly shameful. However, generational change isn’t unconditionally right. We need to create a framework that can unite the people across old, middle-aged, and young generations. More importantly, the party must decide on its overall line—what efforts it will make to realize a democracy proven through the people’s lives.” <<> ―What direction should the Democratic Party’s line take? <<> “I hear people saying they don’t know who the Democratic Party is for. Some call it ‘the party for wealthy leftists in Gangnam,’ while others say, ‘Looking at the party membership, isn’t it a party for people in their 50s?’ They say this because we haven’t shown our intended direction. We must clarify the party’s line and address youth issues within that framework. The party’s overall line should prioritize people’s livelihoods. In particular, if the current government is focusing on expanding the future pie through economic growth policies aligned with the era of change, like AI technology development, then the party should focus on devising measures to ensure the people are not left behind and can thrive equitably in that process. If we fail to handle these issues properly, polarization could become extremely severe by the 2028 general election and the 2030 presidential election. The people can only feel at ease if we make overcoming the increasingly severe asset imbalance and polarization a major party line and focus on discussing solutions intensively.” <<> ―While serving as a Democratic Party lawmaker, was there a ‘moment in politics’ where you thought, ‘We handled that well,’ or that this is the direction to keep going? <<> “The moment I was most proud of as a Democratic Party lawmaker was when we created the Euljiro Committee in 2013 and carried out its activities. Politics must be ‘the weapon of the weak.’ That was exactly the slogan of the Euljiro Committee. As soon as I became a supreme council member in 2013, I went to the field, saw the tears of the so-called ‘Eul’s (weaker parties), and to represent their interests, I went around fighting against the ‘Gap’s (stronger parties).’ While balancing (the unfair Gap-Eul relationship), I felt proud, thinking, ‘Ah, this is the Democratic Party I wanted to be a part of.’ In this recent ‘Homeplus crisis,’ Euljiro Committee Chair Min Byung-deog worked very hard. Initially, MBK Partners, the majority shareholder, and Meritz Financial Group, the largest creditor, had no regard for the livelihoods of 100,000 people (including Homeplus workers, tenant businesses, and supplier partners) and were only interested in quickly bankrupting Homeplus to sell its assets. But when the Democratic Party announced it would hold a Homeplus hearing, they finally came up with a solution, didn’t they? The Euljiro Committee’s activities should be made a major party policy and line. Only then will the people think, ‘Ah, democracy improves my life. I won’t suffer injustice and can be paid fairly for my work.’ I will continue to play that role.” <<> hongbyul@hani.co.kr ( 민주당 전대 후보 등록이 시작된 지난 16일 국회 의원회관에서 만난 우 의원은 “그 어느 때보다 답답하고 무거운 심정”이라고 했다. “불법 비상계엄, 내란이라는 죽을 고비를 국민과 함께 넘기고 이재명 정부가 들어선 지 이제 고작 1년”인데, 서로에게 멸칭을 쓰며 ‘명청대전’이라는 말이 나올 정도로 “내부가 갈라져 권력투쟁을 하는 듯한 모습만 보여주고 있어서”다. 그는 “지금 민주당이 누구를 위한 정당인지를 잘 모르겠다는 말이 나온다”며 “국민들 실망이 커져 (정권 재창출에) 실패하면 다시는 민주 정부를 만들지 못하게 될지도 모른다는 위기감이 든다”고 했다.)

item.title: Kim Bo-mi: “Democratic Party must stop ‘lineage disputes’ and pursue ‘generational shift in power’” (김보미 “민주당, 족보 논쟁 멈추고 ‘권한의 세대교체’ 해야”)
item.description:
“We need a ‘generational shift in power’ where young people can actually exercise decision-making authority. If we keep digging into lineages, engaging in factional and orthodox lineage disputes, and only talking about the past, the Democratic Party will perish. We must transform into a party with a blueprint for the future.” (“청년이 실제로 결정권을 행사할 수 있는 ‘권한의 세대교체’를 해야 한다. 이대로 족보 캐고 계파·적통 논쟁하며 과거 얘기만 하면 민주당은 망한다. 미래의 설계도를 가진 정당으로 탈바꿈해야 한다.”)

Kim Bo-mi (37), the only candidate in her 30s in the race for party leader in the Democratic Party of Korea’s August 17 national convention, emphasized ‘generational shift’ and ‘the future’ in an interview with The Hankyoreh on the 21st. Born in Gangjin County, South Jeolla Province, Kim was elected as the first and youngest female county councilor in Gangjin in the 2018 local elections, and after winning reelection in 2022, served as the youngest chair of a local council in the country. ( 더불어민주당 8·17 전당대회 당대표 선거 후보 중 유일한 30대인 김보미(37) 후보는 21일 한겨레와 한 인터뷰에서 ‘세대교체’와 ‘미래’를 강조했다. 전남광주통합특별시 강진군 출신인 김 후보는 2018년 지방선거에서 최초·최연소 여성 강진군의원으로 당선된 뒤 2022년 재선에 성공해 전국 최연소 기초의회 의장을 지냈다.)

– You strongly criticized the party over the ‘scrapped introduction of an elected youth supreme council member system’ and the ‘controversy over raising candidate deposits for the primary.’ ( ―‘선출직 청년 최고위원제 도입 무산’, ‘경선 후보 기탁금 인상 논란’을 두고 당을 강하게 비판했다.)

“Isn’t this the party’s true feelings (toward youth)? So far, they’ve only used (youth) and made them window dressing. The three candidates who have been in politics for a long time and served in leadership (Kim Min-seok, Cheong Cheong-rae, Song Young-gil) say they will introduce a youth supreme council member system if elected, but I can’t trust them. If I become party leader, I will eliminate the deposit barriers and propose the youth supreme council member system as the first agenda item on the day of my inauguration. The constantly changing primary rules are also a problem. I will change this situation where nothing obvious or basic is being observed.” ( “이게 (청년을 향한) 이 당의 진심이 아닐까. 지금까지 (청년을) 이용만 하고 들러리만 세웠다. 정치 오래하고 지도부도 하셨던 세분 후보(김민석·정청래·송영길)가 당선되면 청년 최고위원제 도입하겠다고 하지만 믿을 수가 없다. 내가 당대표가 되면 기탁금 장벽을 없애고, 청년 최고위원제도 취임 당일 안건 1호로 발의할 것이다. 수시로 바뀌는 경선 룰도 문제다. 당연하고 기본적인 게 하나도 지켜지지 않는 상황을 제가 바꾸겠다.”)

– What is the specific vision for ‘generational shift’? ( ―‘세대교체’의 구체적인 그림은 무엇인가?)

“Everyone shouts about youth, but there are no youth in the party. In this era of calling for becoming one of the three major powers in AI, the ruling party should lead future agendas, but if that generation (the 386 generation) goes with a mindset of milking it as 686, 786, 886, 986, it will all fail. A major reform on the level of re-founding the party is needed. The vested interests must step aside, and the party should be newly structured around youth and experts from future generations. (Other candidates) say they’ll set up committees and appoint youth, but what’s the point? They don’t have any power. Instead of just coming up with slogan-driven or handout-based youth policies, we need to actually give young people ‘power.’ When elected, I will ensure that the party’s youth committee has decision-making authority over youth-related policies. A ‘youth employment guarantee system’ should also be introduced as a core party policy.” ( “모두가 청년을 외치지만 당에는 청년이 없다. 에이아이(AI·인공지능) 3대 강국을 외치는 시대에 여당이 미래 의제를 주도해야 하는데, 그 세대(386세대)가 686, 786, 886, 986까지 해먹겠다는 마인드로 가면 다 망한다. 재창당 수준의 대개혁이 있어야 한다. 기득권은 물러나고 청년과 미래 세대 전문가 중심으로 당을 새롭게 짜야 한다. (다른 후보들이) 위원회를 만들어서 청년을 임명하겠다고 하던데 그럼 뭐 하나, 권한이 없는데. 구호성·시혜성 청년정책만 낼 게 아니라 실제로 청년 당사자에게 ‘권한’을 줘야 한다. 당선되면 청년 관련 정책은 당 청년위가 결정권을 갖게 하겠다. ‘청년 취업 보장제’도 당의 핵심 정책으로 도입해야 한다.”)

– The national convention is overheating with disputes over ‘legitimacy’ and ‘personal politics.’ ( ―전당대회가 ‘정통성’, ‘자기 정치’ 논쟁으로 과열되고 있는데.)

“The president is running ahead with future agendas, but we’re not thinking about supporting and advancing them; instead, we’re holding onto the past, ‘digging up lineages,’ and fighting. The urgent issues of our livelihoods matter now, but we’re fussing over who is the orthodox successor. Youth have no interest. Who cares about debates on prosecutorial reform or supplementary investigative powers? The current competition at the national convention is too disconnected from the people’s lives.” ( “대통령은 미래 의제를 갖고 뛰고 있는데, 뒷받침해 나아갈 생각은 안 하고 과거만 붙잡고 ‘족보 캐기’ 하며 싸우고 있다. 당장 우리가 먹고사는 민생 의제가 중요한데, 적통이니 뭐니 하고 있다. 청년들은 관심 없다. 검찰개혁, 보완수사권 논쟁에도 누가 관심 있나. 지금 전당대회 경쟁은 국민의 삶과는 너무 괴리감이 있다.”)

– What is the role of the next ruling party leader? ( ―차기 여당 대표의 역할은?)

“The first duty is naturally the success of the Lee Jae-myung government and building the foundation for regaining power. We must become a ruling party that prepares future agendas one step ahead of the president. We shouldn’t blindly shield the president’s faults. A ruling party that only claps isolates the president. We must listen to the grassroots sentiment and convey it to the president. I will carry on the spirit of Kim Dae-jung and Roh Moo-hyun, who fought against the odds, and the orthodox lineage of that challenge.” ( “제1임무는 당연히 이재명 정부의 성공이고, 재집권의 토대를 만드는 것이다. 미래 의제를 대통령보다 한발 앞서 준비하는 여당이 돼야 한다. 대통령의 잘못을 무조건 감싸서도 안 된다. 박수만 치는 여당은 대통령을 고립시킨다. 바닥 민심을 경청해 대통령에게 전달해야 한다. 계란으로 바위 치기였던 김대중·노무현의 정신, 그 도전의 적통을 잇겠다.”)

– If you are not included in the final three for the main primary, what are your plans afterward? ( ―본경선 최종 3인에 포함되지 않을 경우, 이후 계획은?)

“Local lawmakers are the closest to the people. People speak most comfortably (to local lawmakers). When I convey these very obvious things (by running in the convention), everyone is astonished, but what I’m saying is really conveying the basics of the basics (of public sentiment). (Regardless of the convention outcome) I will persistently practice breaking the rock of vested interests.” ( “지역 의원이야말로 국민들과 가장 가깝다. 국민들이 (지역 의원에게) 가장 편하게 이야기한다. (전당대회에 출마해서 국민들의) 너무나 당연한 이야기들을 전달하는 데 다들 깜짝 놀라시는데, 제가 말하고 있는 건 정말 (민심의) 기본 중의 기본을 전달하는 것이다. (전대 결과와 상관없이) 기득권 바위 깨기를 꾸준히 실천하겠다.”)

Reporter Kim Chae-un cwk@hani.co.kr ( 김채운 기자 cwk@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Yoon's Office: "New Trump Tariffs Under Section 301 – Industry Minister, Trade Chief to Visit U.S. for Consultations" (청와대 “트럼프 301조 새 관세, 산업장관·통상교섭본부장 미국 방문해 협의”)
item.description:
The presidential office in Seoul stated that regarding the U.S. government's plan to impose new tariffs on dozens of countries, "The Minister of Industry and the Deputy Minister for Trade Negotiations, who will visit the U.S. this week, plan to consult on related matters with the U.S. Department of Commerce and the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR)." (청와대가 수십개국을 상대로 한 미국 정부의 새로운 관세 부과 방침과 관련해 “금주에 방미하는 산업부 장관, 통상교섭본부장이 관련 사항을 미 상무부, 미무역대표부(USTR)와 협의할 계획”이라고 밝혔다.)

The presidential office made this announcement through a press release on the 22nd. U.S. President Donald Trump's 10% 'global tariff,' imposed under reciprocal tariff policies, is set to expire on the 24th following a ruling by the U.S. Supreme Court that deemed such reciprocal tariffs unlawful. Accordingly, the Trump administration is reportedly preparing a new tariff imposition policy based on Section 301 of the Trade Act. The presidential office added, "The U.S. government has consistently stated its position of respecting the Korea-U.S. tariff agreement," and "As the expiration date of the global tariff imposition on July 24 approaches, the government is closely monitoring relevant developments." <<> Reporter Shim Woo-sam wu32@hani.co.kr (청와대는 22일 언론 공지를 통해 이렇게 밝혔다. 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령은 미국 연방대법원의 상호관세 위법 판결로 그간 부과해온 10% ‘글로벌 관세’가 오는 24일 만료되면서, 무역법 301조에 기반한 새로운 관세 부과 방침을 준비 중인 것으로 알려졌다. 청와대는 “미국 정부는 그동안 한미 관세 합의를 존중하겠다는 입장을 표명해왔다”며 “7월24일로 글로벌 관세 부과 종료 시점이 다가오는 만큼 정부는 관련 동향을 기민하게 파악하고 있다”고 덧붙였다.)

item.title: Cheong Wa Dae Recruits 'Youth Fellowship'... President Lee Says "No Fancy Career or Specs Needed" (청와대 ‘청년 펠로우십’ 모집…이 대통령 “거창한 경력·스펙 필요없다”)
item.description:
On the 22nd, President Lee Jae-myung announced the recruitment of the Cheong Wa Dae Youth Fellowship, stating, "We aim to invite you, the youth, not merely as subjects of policy, but as colleagues to ponder together and find answers together." (이재명 대통령이 22일 “청년 여러분을 단지 정책의 대상이 아니라 함께 고민하고 함께 답을 찾아가는 동료로 모시고자 한다”며 청와대 청년 펠로우십을 모집한다고 밝혔다.)

On Facebook that day, the President said, "If a policy affects the lives of youth, its starting point must also be the voices of youth," adding, "While the government is constantly contemplating more delicate and innovative measures, there are clear limitations in capturing all the realities you, the youth, face daily." (이 대통령은 이날 페이스북에 “청년의 삶에 영향을 미치는 정책이라면 그 출발 역시 청년의 목소리여야 한다”며 “정부 또한 더욱 섬세하고 획기적인 방안을 늘 고민하지만, 청년 여러분께서 매일 마주하는 현실을 모두 담아내기에는 분명 한계가 있다”며 이렇게 말했다.)

The President further stated, "A grand career or special specs are not necessary," and "Even a small question felt in daily life is fine, and thoughts like 'I wish it could change this way' are also fine. If you have the desire to create a better world, along with hope and responsibility for the future, that is enough." He added, "We want to see the world through the eyes of youth, talk about policy in the language of youth, and shape the future of the Republic of Korea together based on the experiences of youth," and "We look forward to the keen interest and participation of our youth." (이 대통령은 그러면서 “거창한 경력이나 특별한 스펙은 필요하지 않다”며 “일상에서 느낀 작은 의문도 좋고 ‘이렇게 바뀌면 좋겠다’는 생각도 좋다. 더 좋은 세상을 만들고 싶은 마음, 미래를 향한 희망과 책임감이 있다면 그것만으로 충분하다”고 말했다. 이어 “청년의 시선으로 세상을 바라보고, 청년의 언어로 정책을 이야기하며, 청년의 경험으로 대한민국의 미래를 함께 만들어 가고 싶다”며 “우리 청년 여러분의 많은 관심과 참여를 기대한다”고 덧붙였다.)

The recruitment for the 1st Cheong Wa Dae Youth Fellowship began on the 20th and will run until 6 PM on the 5th of next month. After the announcement of document screening results, the fellows will work from September 1st of this year to February 28th of next year. Eligible applicants are youth aged 19 to 34. (제1기 청와대 청년 펠로우십 모집은 지난 20일 시작돼 다음 달 5일 오후 6시까지 진행된다. 서류심사 결과 발표 등을 거쳐 오는 9월1일부터 내년 2월28일까지 근무하게 된다. 신청 대상은 만 19살 이상 34살 이하 청년이다.)

Reporter Seo Young-ji yj@hani.co.kr (서영지 기자 yj@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Han Byung-do: "Prosecutors Must Investigate Directly to Protect Victims? Looking at the Past, That's Not the Truth" (한병도 “검사가 직접 수사해야 피해자 보호? 과거사 보면 진실 아냐”)
item.description:
Han Byung-do, acting leader of the Democratic Party of Korea and floor leader, said on the 22nd, "The Democratic Party will strengthen the right to request supplementary investigations, and clearly hold investigative agencies accountable to promptly and faithfully fulfill such requests." This signals the party's intention to fully abolish prosecutors' supplementary investigation authority and instead empower the right to request such investigations. (한병도 더불어민주당 당 대표 직무대행 겸 원내대표가 “민주당은 보완수사 요구권을 실질화하고, 수사기관이 그 요구를 신속하고 충실하게 이행하도록 책임을 분명히 하겠다”고 22일 말했다. 검사의 보완수사권을 전면 폐지하고 요구권을 실질화하겠다는 방침을 밝힌 것이다.)

At a Supreme Council meeting held at the National Assembly that day, Floor Leader Han stated, "'Prosecutors do not investigate' is both the starting point and the completion of the prosecution reform that separates investigation from indictment. There is no disagreement within the party on this core principle." Han added, "The discussion has sufficiently matured. Now is the time to unite the party's collective will." (한 원내대표는 이날 국회에서 열린 최고위원회의에서 “‘검사는 수사하지 않는다’는 것이 수사와 기소를 분리하는 검찰개혁의 출발이자 완성이다. 이 대원칙에는 당내 어떠한 이견도 없다”며 이렇게 밝혔다. 한 원내대표는 “논의는 충분히 무르익었다”며 “이제 당의 총의를 하나로 모을 시점”이라고 했다.)

Han further said, "Differences in detailed perceptions should not shake the principle of separating investigation from indictment, nor serve as a means to revive the prosecution's investigative authority. There should only be intense debate to create a better system, such as methods of mutual checks and cooperation among investigative agencies and measures to protect victims." (한 원내대표는 “세부적인 인식의 차이가 수사와 기소의 분리라는 원칙을 흔들거나 검찰의 수사권을 되살리는 수단이 돼선 안 된다”며 “수사기관 간 상호 견제와 협력의 방식, 피해자 보호 대책 등 더 나은 제도를 만들기 위한 치열한 토론만이 있을 뿐”이라고 했다.)

Floor Leader Han remarked, "I have also listened carefully to the argument that supplementary investigation authority is needed to protect victims. I deeply sympathize with the urgent voices that not a single victim should be left behind in the gaps of the system." (한 원내대표는 “피해자 보호를 위해 보완수사권이 필요하다는 주장도 경청했다”며 “단 한 명의 피해자도 제도의 틈에 남겨져선 안 된다는 절박한 목소리에도 깊이 공감한다”고 했다.)

He continued, "That is precisely why victim protection should not be left to the goodwill or discretion of a specific agency. The claim that prosecutors must investigate directly to protect victims is not the truth when we look back at the dark history of the prosecution." (그는 이어 “그렇기에 더더욱 피해자 보호를 특정 기관의 선의나 재량에 맡겨선 안될 것”이라며 “검사가 직접 수사해야만 피해자를 보호할 수 있다는 주장은 지난 검찰의 어두운 과거사를 돌아보면 진실이 아님을 알 수 있다”고 말했다.)

Han stated, "The Democratic Party will strengthen the right to request supplementary investigations and clearly hold investigative agencies accountable to promptly and faithfully fulfill those requests. We will establish mechanisms for control and cooperation that fit the new criminal justice system." (한 원내대표는 “민주당은 보완수사요구권을 실질화하고, 수사기관이 그 요구를 신속하고 충실하게 이행하도록 책임을 분명히 하겠다”며 “새로운 형사사법체계에 맞는 통제와 협력의 장치를 세우겠다”고 했다.)

He added, "We will set up a cross-investigation system where the police and the Major Crimes Investigation Agency check each other, and strengthen investigation reviews and external oversight. We will also more robustly guarantee victims' rights to object, to access records, and to receive legal assistance." (이어 “경찰과 중수청(중대범죄수사청)이 서로를 견제하는 교차수사체계를 세우고 수사심의와 외부 감찰을 강화하겠다. 피해자의 이의신청권과 기록 열람권, 법률 조력을 받을 권리도 더욱 두텁게 보장하겠다”고 했다.)

item.title: Kim Min-seok on Yoo Si-min’s "Fish Market Rotten Smell" Comment: "Just Another Intellectual Changing Course" (김민석, 유시민 “어물전 썩은 내” 발언에…“지식인 변침일 뿐”)
item.description:
Kim Min-seok, a candidate for the leadership of the Democratic Party of Korea, countered author Yoo Si-min’s criticism of the ruling party, in which Yoo said, "If you leave a fish market alone, it’s bound to give off a rotten smell," by stating, "In the language of comrades, there are no words like ‘certain defeat’ or ‘rotten smell’." (김민석 더불어민주당 당대표 후보는 유시민 작가가 “어물전 내버려두면 썩은 내 풍기게 돼 있다”며 여권을 비판한 것에 대해 “동지의 언어에 ‘필패’, ‘썩은 내’라는 단어는 없다”고 반박했다.)

In a Facebook post on the 22nd, Kim said, "The false prophecies predicting certain defeat for the Lee Jae-myung government will fail this time too, just like their bogus predictions that Kim Dae-jung would fail." He added, "Politics that distorts and manipulates the president’s own voice and intentions, crossing the line of commentary, has even lost restraint and dignity," and dismissed Yoo, saying, "Broadly speaking, he’s just another intellectual changing course, like Kim Ji-ha, Cho Soon, or Lee Nak-yon." <<> Yoo appeared on the YouTube show "2-Minute News" the previous night and, while making remarks suggesting that the internal discord within the ruling camp over the prosecution reform process was due to President Lee Jae-myung, said, "Even the finest fish market selling high-quality fish is bound to smell fishy, and if left unchecked with no limits, every fish market is bound to give off a rotten smell." (김 후보는 22일 페이스북에 올린 글에서 “이재명 정부의 필패를 예언하는 헛예언들은 김대중이 실패하리라던 그들의 엉터리 예언처럼 이번에도 필패할 것”이라며 이렇게 말했다. 김 후보는 그러면서 “대통령의 육성과 진심을 왜곡변조하며 평론의 선을 월경한 정치는 절제와 품격조차 놓았다”며 “(유 작가는) 크게 보면 김지하, 조순, 이낙연처럼 또 하나의 지식인 변침일 뿐”이라고 했다.)

Kim said, "The Democratic Party will prevail on both fronts, inside and outside the party," and addressed Yoo, saying, "We will treat the aggressiveness of a return to politics, stripped of the guise of commentary, as a different political opinion and respect it." He added, "If it serves as a backdrop for the Rebuilding Korea Party to strengthen its independent line, we’ll take that into account as well. The Democratic Party will reorganize itself, replace its leadership, and walk the great path befitting a centrist force for solidarity, integration, and expansion." <<> By Lee Ji-eun, reporter jieuny@hani.co.kr (유 작가는 전날 밤 유튜브 방송 ‘2분뉴스’에 출연해 검찰개혁 추진 과정에서 벌어진 여권 내 혼선이 이재명 대통령 때문이라는 취지의 발언을 하면서 “아무리 품질 좋은 생선을 파는 어물전도 비린내가 나기 마련이고, 어떤 제한도 두지 않고 내버려두면 모든 어물전은 썩은 내를 풍기게 돼 있다”고 했다.)

item.title: [Rebuttal Report] Regarding "[Exclusive] "There are many handsome oppas here" – People Power Party's Kim Min-jeon made inappropriate remarks to teenagers in Busan" ([반론보도] 「[단독] “여기 잘생긴 오빠 많아” 국힘 김민전, 부산서 10대에 부적절 발언」 관련)
item.description:
On May 26, 2026, our media outlet published an article on the politics page of The Hankyoreh internet edition titled <[Exclusive] "There are many handsome oppas here" – People Power Party's Kim Min-jeon made inappropriate remarks to teenagers in Busan>. (본 매체는 2026년 5월26일 인터넷 한겨레 정치면에 <[단독] “여기 잘생긴 오빠 많아” 국힘 김민전, 부산서 10대에 부적절 발언>이라는 제목의 기사를 보도하였습니다. )

In response, Representative Kim Min-jeon's office stated that "the term 'oppa' was not used to refer to candidate Park Min-sik or any politician of a similar age." ( 이에 대해 김민전 의원 쪽은 “박민식 후보나 비슷한 연배의 정치인을 두고 ‘오빠’라고 지칭한 것이 아니다”라고 알려왔습니다.)

This report is issued in accordance with the mediation of the Press Arbitration Commission. ( 이 보도는 언론중재위원회의 조정에 따른 것입니다.)
